primary_claim: STACK, a method that attacks each layer of a multi-layer AI defense pipeline sequentially, achieves a 71% attack success rate against a Gemma-2 few-shot classifier defense on the catastrophic-risk ClearHarm dataset (limited-feedback setting), compared to 0% for conventional jailbreak attacks like PAP against the same defense.

effect.value: 71% (STACK, limited-feedback) vs 0% (conventional attacks e.g. PAP); 33% for STACK in a black-box transfer setting

contradicts_or_qualifies: Questions whether low attack success rates of multi-layer defenses against conventional attacks reflect true robustness, or merely that those attacks were not designed to penetrate multi-layered defenses
stated_future_work: Testing STACK variants on production systems like Claude 4 Opus to evaluate real-world resilience
Continued research into both attack and defense methodologies to determine how far defense-in-depth can scale
Avoid revealing which component blocked a request by ensuring consistent response times and formats across all rejection types
Maintain strict separation between production models used as input/output filters and publicly available models
limitations_stated: Test pipelines do not perfectly replicate commercial systems' implementations and used models likely smaller than production systems, without extensive data generation techniques like those in constitutional classifiers
A 15% false positive rate was allowed, far higher than practical systems could tolerate
Tests focused on weapons-related harmful content using English-language queries only
The 71% success rate assumes attackers know which component blocked their request, information that could be withheld
quote: STACK achieves a 71% success rate in causing our defended model to answer harmful questions on a catastrophic risk dataset ClearHarm. By contrast, conventional attacks achieved 0% success against the same defenses.
